title: Delegated Discount Approval + Security-Questionnaire (SQ) Gating Experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
body: Goal: reduce deal cycle time and maintain margin discipline by delegating routine discount approvals to quota owners while gating larger or higher-risk discounts behind a security-questionnaire (SQ) scoring threshold and a lightweight central review. This ticket scopes a pilot A/B experiment, the approval delegation matrix, pricebook update requirements, and the SQ gating rules that should automatically escalate approvals for risky profiles. Background: current approvals for enterprise discounts require manual review by pricing ops/legal for almost all non-list adjustments, causing ~3-7 day median delay on deals >$50k ARR. There is no consistent linkage between Salesforce opportunity risk (security posture from SQ) and approval routing. We propose: 1) A delegation matrix that allows Sales leaders and assigned AE managers to approve up to defined bands (by ARR, product surface, and term length) without central pricing ops review. 2) An SQ score threshold that forces escalation for deals that touch sensitive features (on-prem, private deployment, KMS/HSM usage) or score above a risk threshold. 3) An experiment that randomizes eligible deals into (A) delegated-approval path and (B) centralized-pricing-path to measure cycle time, win-rate, and net revenue impact over 8 weeks. 4) Pricebook canonicalization: map enterprise SKUs/discount bands into machine-readable pricebook entries to avoid manual adjustments and support audit logs. 5) Minimal engineering surface: an approval API endpoint, an SQ webhook to annotate SF opportunities, and audit logging to meet finance and compliance needs.
acceptance_criteria: Delegation matrix drafted and signed off by Sales, Finance, and Legal
SQ gating rules defined with numeric thresholds and example mappings for 'on-prem', 'VPC', 'HSM', and 'sensitive data' flags
Experiment design doc published with success metrics (cycle time reduction, ARR lift/loss, win-rate delta) and statistical plan
Pricebook entries updated with canonical discount bands and machine tags for automation
Engineering tickets created for approval API, SQ webhook, and audit trail; estimates attached
Pilot launched on a defined sales segment with monitoring dashboards (Looker/Grafana) and weekly reports
comments: 2025-02-21 — Aisha: Initial scoping call with Sales Ops, Finance, Legal. Agreement to pilot on mid-market enterprise segment (ARR 25k-250k) and exclude critical-regulated customers in first run.

2025-02-24 — Marco: Drafted delegation matrix. Proposal: AE Manager approves up to 10% discount for committed term <=24 months; Head of Sales approves up to 25% for ARR <100k; Pricing Ops retains overrides and can rescind delegation for named accounts.

2025-02-26 — Legal (S. Kim): SQ gating must include precise language for on-prem/HSM usage; we need a clause for 'sensitive controls' that flags the contract for full legal review. Legal requests example SQ responses mapped to gating buckets.

2025-03-01 — Finance (L. Chen): Recommend revenue-protecting guardrails: floor price enforcement in the pricebook and automated alerts when delegated approval reduces margin by >20% relative to list price. Also need audit fields for month-end review.

2025-03-03 — Eng (R. Osei): We can build the approval API and webhook in 3 sprints. Raised ENG-9812 for approval API and ENG-9934 for SQ webhook and migration of pricebook tags. Raised question about storing SQ results vs. ephemeral annotation — Legal prefers retained evidence for audits.

2025-03-04 — Product (Aisha): Experiment design updated with sample size estimates. Expect to need ~200 eligible opportunities to detect a 12-hour median cycle-time improvement with 80% power. Tracking fields in SF: 'delegation_path', 'sq_score', 'approval_latency', 'final_discount_pct'.
2025-03-05 — Sales Ops (K. Alvarez): Agreed to run pilot in US region only and on deals with single-product SKUs to reduce confounders. Will provide CSV of eligible opps and map to AE managers.
2025-03-05 — Decision: move forward with pilot after legal finalizes SQ gating mapping; engineering to prioritize approval API on next sprint and product to publish playbook for pilot.
decision_summary: Approve pilot A/B experiment to test delegated approvals vs central pricing on mid-market enterprise deals with SQ gating; engineering will deliver minimal API/webhook surface and pricebook canonicalization. Legal must sign off SQ gating mappings before launch.
next_steps: Legal: publish SQ gating mapping spreadsheet with example responses (due 2025-03-10)
Engineering: create ENG-9812 (approval API) and ENG-9934 (SQ webhook) and attach estimates (sprint planning 2025-03-06)
Product: finalize experiment doc and publish to Confluence (due 2025-03-07)
Sales Ops: provide list of eligible opportunities and AE manager mapping (due 2025-03-07)
Finance: implement margin alert logic in pricebook tooling and configure monthly review report (due 2025-03-14)
Launch: target pilot start date 2025-03-17 pending legal sign-off and engineering readiness
